explanations: rejectsStartWhenPlanLimitReached verifies that save is never called, but start() never calls save at all: new sessions are persisted with insert, and save is only used by heartbeat(). The verification can never fail, so it adds no protection. A regression that writes the new session via insert before throwing the limit exception would still pass. The check should be verify(store, never()).insert(any()).

B is right: the fixed clock pins NOW and the id supplier returns "s-new", so tests can assert equality and build sessions 30 seconds or 10 minutes old. A is wrong because the mocks and fixed values are unrelated to parallelism. C is wrong because the stores are still mocked. D is wrong because HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT is a constant.

D is right: with a limit of 1 and one ten-minute-old session, counting it makes start() throw. In startsSessionWhenUnderLimit the one session is live and the limit is 2. heartbeatStoresCurrentTime does not call start(). The resume test returns before the limit check.

A is right: the test asserts neither a heartbeat update nor the stored timestamp. B would throw ConcurrentStreamLimitException because the limit is 1. C is caught by verify(store, never()).insert(any()). D is caught by assertSame.
